risks.basis: THIS FILE has a confirmed defect on record
risks.risk: alf_mar append-only TOCTOU: the handler SELECTed for an existing entry_id, answered 409 ALREADY_RECORDED if found, then POSTed with Prefer: resolution=merge-duplicates. Two callers racing the SAME entry_id could both pass the SELECT before either POST landed, and the second POST's merge-duplicates resolution silently OVERWROTE the first row instead of reaching the 409 -- a recorded medication administration of 'given' replaced by 'refused', unrecoverably, with no error anywhere. Fixed by routing through public.alf_check_and_insert_mar_entry(), which holds pg_advisory_xact_lock across the check and the write in one transaction.

risks.basis: THIS FILE has a confirmed defect on record
risks.risk: bld_draws retainage release lost update: the branch read the draw's jsonb data, computed a new retainage_released and appended one audit entry to retainage_release_log client-side, then PATCHed the whole blob back with only license_hash and draw_id in the WHERE clause -- no version or CAS predicate. Two concurrent release_retainage calls on the same draw each read the same starting value and whichever PATCH landed second silently won, discarding the first release's figure AND its audit-trail entry with no error. Fixed by routing through public.bld_release_retainage_atomic(), an optimistic-CAS RPC that compares the row's current retainage_released against what the caller read under pg_advisory_xact_lock and raises RETAINAGE_RELEASE_CONFLICT rather than overwriting blind.

Three arms asserted a flat 403 for caregiver/med_aide/activities reads, which api/sd-data.js:10739 deliberately stopped answering on 2026-09-27 when a care role was given a self-scoped read of its own filings -- AND the suite's own fetch mock ignored the '&recorded_by=eq.<session.employee_id>' clause the handler adds for non-broad roles, returning every row to every caller. Found only because the suite was red for an unrelated reason -- the absent-expectedApp stub shape shared by 12 files since c8b5e5b1 -- and clearing that exposed three survivors.

risks.basis: the same app (sairncare) has this defect on record
risks.risk: api/sd-data.js read SIX SAIRNcare append-only trails with no order= clause -- alf_mar, alf_incidents, alf_signals, alf_claim_routes, alf_staff_credentials, alf_op_audits. Postgres promises nothing about the order of a SELECT that does not ask for one and PostgREST forwards that through, so rows came back in plan order. On a small table a seq scan usually returns heap order, which is why it looked like insertion order for the whole of development and would stop the first time the planner picked an index. WORST INSTANCE, and the one the severity is set by: prRenderRecorded maps alf_claim_routes rows straight into a table with NO client sort of any kind and renders created_at sliced to 10 characters, so the server order WAS the display order and there was none -- a billing determination trail in arbitrary order. alf_mar and alf_incidents do sort, but on a date-only jsonb field, so every same-day entry ties and falls back to server order under a stable sort. alf_staff_credentials and alf_op_audits already sorted by created_at desc client-side and were deterministic except on an exact tie. alf_signals has no consumer yet. THE INJECTION COMMIT NAMED IS f29e5f95, the claim_routes instance; the other five entered in separate commits and the lag here is that one instance's, not the class's.

risks.basis: the same app (sairncare) has this defect on record
risks.risk: api/_lib/compliance-rules.js evaluateTraining()'s optional per-staff branch answered meets:TRUE for a staff member with ZERO recorded training hours, in a state that mandates them. Driven 2026-09-26 against the real committed seed: West Virginia, staff member with annual_hours_recorded 0, returned { required_annual_hours: 0, recorded_annual_hours: 0, shortfall_hours: 0, meets: TRUE, applicable_requirements: [null, null] }. WV mandates 8 hours a year for an administrator and 2 hours a year of dementia training for ALL staff under 64 CSR 14. Its requirement rows are shaped {audience, hours_per_year, topic}; this branch reads r.who and r.annual_hours, so every requirement contributed Number(undefined) || 0 and the applicable_requirements array came back as [null, null]. A DIFFERENT VOCABULARY WAS READ AS AN EMPTY ONE, and once summed an empty requirement set is indistinguishable from a satisfied one. A SECOND FABRICATION SURVIVES A CORRECT VOCABULARY AND IS WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: Pennsylvania rows carry additive:true, a secured-dementia-unit requirement ON TOP OF the general annual hours, so collapsing 12 general and 6 dementia into one target of 18 and comparing one recorded total meant a staff member with 18 hours of general training and no dementia training read as compliant -- UNDER-requires, a false PASS; and Ohio rows carry counts_toward_general_annual:true, 4 and 8 hours that count TOWARD the general 8 rather than adding to it, so summing all four rows produced a required total of 29 where the code requires less -- OVER-requires, a false FAIL, which is the merciful direction and is still a wrong number on a compliance board. Both fields are machine-readable and present on the real seeded rows; nothing was reading either. THE BRANCH HAS NEVER FIRED: sairncare.html's cqShowTraining() sends {state, facility_class, requirement_type} and no staff array, so the whole branch is dormant and none of this has reached a screen -- which is the only reason this is a latent defect rather than an incident, and is not a reason to leave it, because the open request that surfaced it was to BUILD the caller. FIXED BY REFUSING RATHER THAN GUESSING, matching this module's own stated standard that nothing is ever silently substituted: a requirement row carrying neither `who` nor `annual_hours` now returns REQUIREMENTS_NOT_JOINABLE naming the state, the rule and the unreadable rows' key sets; and any applicable requirement carrying stacking semantics (additive, counts_toward_general_annual, or an explicit stacking field) now yields meets:null with a meets_unknown_reason rather than a boolean in either direction, while still reporting the recorded and required figures. Measured across all six seeded training rules after the fix: OH null, IN false, MI not applicable, PA/alr null, PA/pch null, WV refused -- one of six states can currently be answered at all.

risks.basis: the same app (sairncare) has this defect on record
risks.risk: api/sd-data.js, alf_claim_routes and alf_staff_credentials: a caller could choose who is recorded as having made the decision. Both reads spread the stored blob LAST over FIVE mapped columns -- Object.assign({ id, resident_id, service_month, decided_by, created_at }, x.data) at :10555 and Object.assign({ id, staff_id, record_type, recorded_by, created_at }, x.data) at :10922 -- while both write paths stripped only THREE keys from the payload before storing it. So a payload carrying `decided_by` (or `recorded_by`) was kept inside `data` and OVERRODE on read the column the server had set from session.employee_id. `created_at` shadowed the same way on both, so the displayed timestamp of the record could also be chosen by the caller. Each write's own echo has the identical spread-last shape, so the forged attribution came straight back in the 200 as well, making the response look like confirmation. WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN AN ORDINARY FIELD LEAK: both tables are APPEND-ONLY BY DESIGN and each branch's 409 message states the reason -- "a completed-training assertion that could be quietly edited later is not evidence of anything". The record could not be edited after the fact; its ATTRIBUTION could be chosen at the moment of writing. alf_staff_credentials is the staff credential and training-hours trail (a regulated attestation about a named person); alf_claim_routes records how a real claim was billed, so the forged field names who made a money determination. FIXED by routing both through api/_lib/blob.js's storedBlob() with the column list derived from each branch's own read -- five keys each, not three. THE PLATFORM ALREADY KNEW THIS SHAPE: alf_op_audits carries a comment saying its read spreads columns LAST precisely so a client-supplied `passed` cannot override the server's computation, and the 2026-09-24 ALF review fixed the `created_at` half on alf_mar and alf_incidents. These two branches were not swept then. alf_signals -- same read shape, four mapped columns, four stripped -- is the branch that got it right, so four ALF branches produced three different outcomes from one pattern.

risks.basis: the same app (sairncare) has this defect on record
risks.risk: BILLING READ ANY RESIDENT'S FULL MEDICATION ADMINISTRATION RECORD THROUGH A SIBLING RESOURCE, AND IT WAS THE THIRD DOOR THE SAME ROLE FOUND TO THE SAME DATA. `alf_mar` -- the resource that OWNS the table -- has refused billing on both read and write since it was written (ALF_MAR_ROLES = {owner, nursing, med_aide}). But the `alf_family_contacts` action `family_mar` gated on ALF_FAMILY_READ_ROLES = {owner, billing, nursing}, so a billing clerk 403'd from the MAR directly received a named resident's whole MAR by asking for that resident's family contact -- and because billing is in the BROAD half of that set the assignment scope was skipped entirely, so it was every resident on the licence, not one. Prior two doors: 2026-10-05 H1 #877, where family_mar had NO caller gate at all and was fixed by inheriting read's role set, which is how billing arrived; and 2026-10-07 7ed27c5e, where derive_charges handed billing the medication NAME for every dose for a month. The #877 author declared this and declined to narrow it in passing, correctly -- a gate disagreeing with its sibling was the defect being repaired -- and flagged it instead. Fixed by giving family_mar its OWN set (ALF_FAMILY_MAR_ROLES = {owner, nursing}) rather than narrowing the contact LIST's set, because the decision was about the MAR and a business office still has to be able to ring a resident's daughter about an invoice. Billing now gets in only through a named, time-limited, audited grant made by an office_manager, expiring at READ time. 28 arms green from 8 passed / 16 failed / 4 unproven; ablated four ways.
